sentences.text: United India Insurance Company Limited vs Kariveda Manemma

Author: Lalitha Kanneganti
Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
 The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 M.A.C.M.A.No.3891 of 2008
Judgment:

This is an appeal filed by the insurance company aggrieved by the award dated 09.02.2007 in O.P.No.38 of 2006 passed by the Chairman, Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-District Judge at Karimnagar.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-District Judge at Karimnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Having heard Mr. V. Srinivasa Rao, learned counsel for the Insurance Company and Mr. N.
Gnaneshwar Rao, learned counsel for the claimant, perused the entire material on record.
3. The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the motor vehicle accident.

The Court below has awarded an amount of Rs.1,32,834/-.
4.
The case of the Insurance Company is that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid driving license at the time of accident and a case was registered under Sec.181 of MV Act.

When the same plea was taken before the Court below, the Court below has observed that the vehicle was insured with the insurance company and the policy is in force and basing on the police record it is stated that driver of the vehicle is not LK, J MACMA_3891_2008 having valid driving license.
Further in the cross examination of Rw.1 on behalf of the insurance company he admitted that he had not issued any notice to the owner of the vehicle to produce driving license.

5. The Court below has observed that except basing on the FIR that the crime was registered under Section 181 of MV Act, no other evidence is adduced by the Insurance Company to show that the owner of the vehicle was not having any valid driving license and has held that Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation.
The same grounds were reiterated by the learned Counsel by the Insurance Company before this Court.

6. The court below has rightly observed that without adducing any evidence, the Insurance Company basing on the crime registered under Section 181 of MV Act is claiming that they are not liable to pay the compensation.
The Court below has rightly dealt the issue and held the Insurance Company liable to pay the compensation.
7. In that view of the mater, this court is not inclined to interfere with the award passed by Tribunal.
